candidates.api_shape: geneva_internal(slots, crank_r, pin_d, thickness, ...) -> {driver, wheel} plus geneva_internal_angle(slots, crank_r) -> wheel_angle(theta)
candidates.fdm: Two flat plates, same pin-and-crescent construction as geneva_pair. The wheel is an annulus. Prints flat. Need a sweep-clear check like _geneva_sweep_clear.
candidates.name: geneva_internal
candidates.why: Driver lives inside the slotted wheel. Motion occupies more than 180 deg of crank, so dwell is the short part (opposite of external). Textbook sibling of geneva_pair; same closed-form layout with inverted centres. Film, turrets, any index that wants a long move and a short lock.

candidates.api_shape: grooved_plate_cam(base_r, segments, groove_w, thickness, roller_r, pin_phase_deg) -> {cam, pin}
candidates.fdm: Extrude the pitch curve as a slot of groove_w through a disc. Same motion-law segments. Print flat. Pin or roller sits in the groove, same as barrel_cam's pin.
candidates.name: grooved_plate_cam
candidates.why: Box / track / closed plate cam: a slot in the plate captures a roller so the follower is form-closed. plate_cam is force-closed (needs roller_follower + spring). Positive drive is the usual request once people have hit follower bounce.

candidates.api_shape: linear_cam(length, lift, segments_or_wedge, thickness, travel) -> {cam, follower}; linear_cam_lift(s)
candidates.fdm: A flat plate or a triangular wedge, optional groove. Prints flat. Pose is travel along the guide. Pair with roller_follower or a sliding pin.
candidates.name: linear_cam
candidates.why: Translating / wedge cam: the cam body strokes in a straight line, follower rides a 2D profile or a wedge. Key duplicators, trip hammers, lock pins, any time the prime mover is already linear. Not a rotary plate_cam with a different argument.

candidates.api_shape: conjugate_cam_pair(base_r, segments, yoke_c, roller_r, clearance, thickness, phase_deg) -> {cam_rise, cam_return, yoke, rollers}
candidates.fdm: Two plates keyed in phase plus a yoke and two rollers. All print flat. Running clearance is a parameter (FDM wants 0.2-0.4 mm, not the metal 20 um). Same MOTION_LAWS as plate_cam.
candidates.name: conjugate_cam_pair
candidates.why: Two complementary plate profiles on one shaft, yoke with two rollers, r1(theta)+r2(theta)=C-2R-delta. Desmodromic / positive-return without a groove. Weaving, cartoners, parallel-index guts, Ducati-style close. Cannot be faked by calling plate_cam twice: the second profile is determined by the first.

candidates.fdm: One flat plate, constant-width profile, prints on its face. Yoke is two flats or two rollers at fixed separation.
candidates.name: constant_breadth_cam
candidates.why: One plate of constant width between two parallel flats (Reuleaux / two-circular-arc family). A single-body desmodromic: the yoke cannot lose contact. Teaching set and a cheap positive-return when you do not want two cams.

candidates.api_shape: globoidal_index_cam(stops, cam_r, roller_d, index_deg, dwell_frac, phase_deg) -> {cam, turret, rollers} plus globoidal_index_angle(phase)
candidates.fdm: Coarse FDM can print the globoid as a lofted rib and the turret as a hub of roller pins (Thingiverse 'scroll cam box' / Grahovski GrabCAD). Not a 5-axis ground metal cam; clearance will be sloppy. Still a valid semi-primitive if the generator emits cam + turret + rollers posed at one index, plus an angle law.
candidates.name: globoidal_index_cam
candidates.why: Ferguson / roller-gear / globoidal indexer: a concave globoid rib (or groove) drives rollers on a turret whose axis is at 90 deg. Sankyo/CAMCO class. The 3D analog of Geneva with programmable accel and a long dwell. Distinct from barrel_cam (cylinder + one axial pin) and from geneva_pair (planar pin-in-slot).

candidates.api_shape: barrel_indexer(stops, radius, length, roller_d, dwell_frac, phase_deg) -> {barrel, turret, rollers} plus barrel_index_angle(phase)
candidates.fdm: Reuse barrel_cam's groove loft, add a turret of roller pins around a perpendicular (or parallel-end) axis. Print barrel standing, turret flat. Thingiverse scroll-cam boxes are this kit.
candidates.name: barrel_indexer
candidates.why: Cylindrical indexing cam: a barrel groove (or ridge) drives a ring of rollers on a turret, not a single translating pin. Nolte/Sankyo 'barrel cam indexer'. barrel_cam already programs one pin in z(theta); this programs theta_out(theta_in) with dwells. Same relationship geneva_pair has to a random slotted disc.

candidates.api_shape: spherical_geneva(slots, sphere_r, pin_d, thickness) -> {driver, wheel} plus spherical_geneva_angle
candidates.fdm: Two printed spherical sectors or thick discs with a pin. Axis concurrency is the same pain as spherical_four_bar. Educational and compact-indexer use.
candidates.name: spherical_geneva
candidates.why: Geneva on a sphere: pin and slots live on concentric spheres, axes concurrent. Wikipedia's third variant. Compact right-angle index. Not internal/external planar Geneva and not globoidal (globoidal is a cam-and-roller, not a pin-in-slot).

candidates.api_shape: grooved_face_cam(radius, segments, groove_w, groove_d, pin_phase_deg) -> {cam, pin}
candidates.fdm: Disc with a milled-style slot of groove_w, prints on its back. Pin sits in the groove. Closed curve required so the slot does not run off the disc.
candidates.name: grooved_face_cam
candidates.why: Slot in the face of a disc, follower moves radially (Wikipedia face-cam, grooved heart). face_cam in-tree is an axial hill, spring-held. barrel_cam is a groove on the cylinder wall. The radial face-groove is the remaining textbook plate.

candidates.api_shape: compose conjugate_cam_pair with a turret, or parallel_index_cam(stops, ...)
candidates.fdm: Two flat cams and a turret of rollers. Prints. Commercial CF3 indexers are housed products.
candidates.name: parallel_index_cam
candidates.why: Two conjugate plate cams + a roller turret, input and output shafts parallel. After conjugate_cam_pair exists this is mostly that pair plus a turret pose. A thin kit is useful; a second full surface generator is not.

candidates.fdm: Same plate, plus a linear driver. Prints.
candidates.name: inverse_cam
candidates.why: Reuleaux inversion: the 'follower' is driven, the cam plate is the output. Useful when the prime mover is a cylinder or solenoid. The profile is the same geometry read backwards; a pose wrapper around plate_cam plus a sliding driver may be enough.

candidates.name: polynomial_motion_laws
candidates.why: 3-4-5, 4-5-6-7, modified trapezoid, harmonic combinants. Extensions of MOTION_LAWS / cam_lift, not a new solid. Worth doing when a globoidal or conjugate kit needs finite jerk; not a part on its own.

candidates.name: maltese_cross
candidates.why: Alias of a 4-slot external Geneva. geneva_pair(slots=4) is the Maltese cross. Do not ship a second name.

candidates.name: star_wheel_geneva
candidates.why: star_wheel in-tree is a packaging pocket wheel for bottles/cans, not a Geneva star. The Geneva star is geneva_pair.

candidates.api_shape: missing: intermittent_gear_angle, not a new mesh
candidates.name: intermittent_gears
candidates.why: Already intermittent_gear_pair (mutilated gear + locking segment). left_out_notes: no engagement pose law. That is an animate-coverage problem, not a missing solid.

candidates.fdm: The table plate is a project part.
candidates.name: ratchet_index_table
candidates.why: Rotary table with a ratchet and a detent. Product assembled from ratchet_wheel_pawl + detent_pair + a frame. The two primitives already exist.

candidates.name: plate_face_barrel_heart_snail
candidates.why: Already plate_cam, face_cam, barrel_cam, heart_cam, snail_cam, cam_lift, cam_profile_2d, roller_follower, swash_plate, eccentric_cam_clamp.

rejected.name: camco_ferguson_housing
rejected.why: Commercial globoidal indexer gearbox (CAMCO RGD, Sankyo roller-gear). Product. The reusable part is globoidal_index_cam.

rejected.name: rotary_index_table_machine
rejected.why: Housed assembly table with cam box, output flange, and station plate. Product.

rejected.name: desmodromic_engine
rejected.why: Ducati valve train as a whole engine. The reusable part is conjugate_cam_pair.

rejected.name: geneva_stop
rejected.why: Watch stop-work / count wheel. Clockwork slice, not a cam/indexer kit.

rejected.name: knife_flat_followers
rejected.why: Follower *styles* on plate_cam (roller_r=0 is already the knife/flat pitch curve). Not separate solids; roller_follower covers the pivoted roller.

sources: .claude/overnight/catalog.json public_api (plate_cam, snail_cam, heart_cam, barrel_cam, face_cam, roller_follower, swash_plate, geneva_pair, geneva_wheel_angle, escapement, intermittent_gear_pair, detent_pair, star_wheel, ratchet_wheel_pawl) + categories cams/indexing + animate demo_*cam/demo_geneva_pair + left_out_notes on intermittent_gear_pair
summary:
A cam is a higher pair that programs a follower from a displacement diagram. Textbooks (Rothbart, Norton, CMU ch.6, Wikipedia) split the family first by the moving surface, then by how the follower is kept on it. Shape class: plate/disc/radial (exists as plate_cam + cam_profile_2d + MOTION_LAWS dwell/linear/shm/cycloidal), face/end/crown (exists as face_cam: raised axial track, spring-held pin), barrel/cylindrical (exists as barrel_cam: closed groove on the drum wall, positive-drive pin), heart (exists, constant-velocity / reset cam), snail/drop (exists), swash plate (exists, spatial analog), linear/translating/wedge (missing: input is a stroke, not a turn; key-duplicator and trip-hammer form), grooved/box/track plate (missing: a slot in the plate so the follower is form-closed, no spring), grooved face (missing: radial slot in a disc face; Wikipedia's 'most common face cam'; distinct from face_cam's axial hill), conjugate/desmodromic pair (missing: two complementary plates on one shaft, yoke captured, r1+r2=C; Ducati/Sulzer/Bosch; also the guts of a parallel indexer), constant-breadth / Reuleaux (missing: one plate of constant width between two flats, a cheap desmodromic), inverse cam (missing: Reuleaux inversion, follower drives, cam is the output), globoidal/Ferguson/roller-gear (missing: concave globoid rib + turret rollers, right-angle indexer), barrel indexer (missing: barrel_cam groove driving a roller turret rather than one translating pin), parallel-index cam (missing: two conjugate plates + turret, shafts parallel). Follower class already has roller_follower; knife and flat-face are arguments, not kits. Motion-law extras (3-4-5 polynomial, modified trapezoid, 4-5-6-7) are segment types for cam_lift, not parts.

Intermittent / indexing is the other half of this slice. External Geneva / Maltese cross is geneva_pair + geneva_wheel_angle (animated; usecase already says 'indexing tables'). star_wheel is a packaging pocket wheel, not a Geneva. intermittent_gear_pair is the mutilated-gear + lock-segment pair (no engagement law in-tree). escapement / escapement_pose is the clock form (animated). detent_pair and ratchet_wheel_pawl cover click-in and one-way click. Missing Geneva variants: internal (driver inside the wheel, motion >180 deg of crank, dwell shorter than motion) and spherical (axes meet, 3D Maltese). Geneva stop / count-wheel is clockwork (other slice). A ratchet-index *table* is a product assembled from ratchet + detent + frame.

Catalog categories already name cams and indexing. Animate covers plate/face/barrel/heart/snail, geneva_pair, swash_plate, eccentric_cam_clamp. left_out_notes call out intermittent_gear_pair as having no pose law (unlike geneva_wheel_angle). Grep of mechlib/cams.py, indexing.py, ratchets.py, usecases.py finds no globoidal, Ferguson, desmodromic, conjugate cam, inverse cam, wedge/linear cam, internal Geneva, or spherical Geneva.
title: Cam types and intermittent motion
